amendments.body: In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:557-559` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:632`, remove the hidden `.max(0.01)` fallback or replace it with explicit zero handling. The new validation path now accepts `temp_condition_min_factor = 0.0`, but molt cadence still silently treats that as `0.01`, so a configuration that is supposed to set the cadence floor to zero will still advance molt readiness and eventually resolve molts instead of freezing readiness.
amendments.rationale: This is a real behavior mismatch introduced by the change: the code now advertises zero as a valid runtime value, but the daily molt path does not honor it. That makes long-run tuning and save/load round-tripping incorrect for zero-floor configurations.

amendments.body: In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1380-1440`, gate `critical_gh_failure` on `params.gh_min_d > 0.0`, matching the new guard added in `molt_cycle`. Right now, when `gh_min_d` is disabled (`0.0`), a failed molt at `GH=0` will still emit a bogus `critical GH ratio` detail even though the success/failure path no longer treats GH as a hard fail in that mode.
amendments.rationale: The patch fixed the runtime hard-fail check but left the failure diagnostics on the old logic. That produces incorrect event provenance for the newly supported zero-minimum configuration.

payload.summary: Reviewed the diff and related molting code/tests end-to-end. I found 2 correctness issues: zero `temp_condition_min_factor` is accepted but not actually honored by molt cadence, and the GH hard-fail diagnostic path was not updated to match the new zero-minimum guard.
